name: Macroeconomic Stabilisation
description:
The 2026 Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences went to researchers Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford for their research on microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilisation.

Join Chetan Ghate for a lecture reviewing the body of work by the laureates that led to them being awarded the prize in this area. The discussion will explore the relevance of their work in macroeconomic policy making as well as its importance in shaping macroeconomic policy frameworks for India. Be sure to attend this insightful session to learn more and to ask Chetan questions about his own work.

name: Namma Oota: Day 2
description:
The Namma Oota festival, hosted by Science Gallery Bengaluru, fuses art, science, and gastronomy.

From what grows in our fields to what lands on our plates, food connects us to questions of ecology, health, culture, and innovation. In the fourth edition of Namma Oota, we hope to explore these curiosities in relation to our diets, communities, and the Anthropocene.

Join us to enjoy the food stalls as we create a flea market-esque ambience with workshops, performances, interactive demonstrations and an open mic to explore. The portico will come alive with the sizzle of tawas, buzzing conversation, and a bit of organised chaos. The festival is curated as a platform to spark conversations and connections on Bengaluru, Oota (food), and sustainability.

name: Heat and Electron Transport: Quantum Signatures
description: The transport properties of materials is a question of fundamental interest to scientists as well as engineers. Some basic questions are: how good is a material for transporting energy and electrons from one region to another? and; can we predict the transport properties of a given material if we are given all the microscopic details of the constituent atoms? Join Abhishek Dhar as he answers these questions and describes the role of quantum mechanics in transport theory along with the surprises it throws.

name: Atoms at Work
description: Join Sagar Sutradhar and Nilanjan Kundu for an exclusive visit to QuMiX Lab, the neutral-atom quantum mixture laboratory, headed by Saptarishi Chaudhuri at Raman Research Institute. Discover how India's first neutral-atom quantum computer is taking shape, explore active quantum mixture experiments, and attend researcher-led mini-talks offering a rare, close-up look at the technology and physics driving the National Quantum Mission.

name: Open Mic @ Namma Oota
description:
Join us for an open mic where storytellers, musicians, comedians, poets and singers come together to celebrate the magic of flavours and melodies. We have a vibrant lineup for the evening, spanning everything from a stand-up act starring a man who stands trial for loving Indo-Chinese food to a spoken word performance by a life sciences scholar. 

If this sounds like your jam, we have open mic spots up for grabs on the day. Whether it’s a nostalgia-soaked recipe, a comical culinary mishap, or a poem about unlikely flavour combinations, this is your opportunity to take the stage and share your love of food with a passionate audience. 

The mic is yours!

name: The Journey Along the Memory Lane—spinning my way
description:
Information storage has been around for thousands of years–initially as cave paintings and carvings. Over the millennia it was done on stone, wood, ceramic and eventually on to paper. The seismic shift took place in the 20th century as it moved onto magnetic tapes, discs revolutionising the data storage and communication. 

With the explosion of information generated, and the demand for ever increasing data storage capacity, accompanied by escalating energy needs puts severe strain on energy infrastructure and environment. A potential direction could be via utilising the exotic properties of superconductors to advance future storage and computing technology—a way forward for lower energy operation while reducing our footprint on nature. 

Join Jagadeesh S. Moodera for the talk, in which he will touch upon his journey along the memory path during his years of fundamental scientific research highlighting the evolution of magnetic data storage. The talk will lead you over his years of evolution in this field—how curiosity and quest for knowledge led to the present, and perhaps into the future.

This lecture is organised in collaboration with International Centre for Theoretical Sciences (ICTS – TIFR).

name: Strange Loop x Tarang Joseph
description: In this set, guitarist Adesh Vinod and singer-songwriter Tarang Joseph build music from scratch, layering guitar riffs, basslines, beats, keys and vocals using electronic music equipment. Drawing on soul and R&B, with influences from artists like Stevie Wonder, Daniel Caesar, Frank Ocean, and Kaytranada, the duo blends live instrumentation with electronic sounds to create something entirely their own. Because it's all looped live, no two sets come out quite the same!

name: Is the Future of Computing Quantum?
description:
Quantum computing has captured the imagination of scientists, technology enthusiasts and the wider public. Promising to tackle computational challenges beyond the reach of today’s classical computers, it has opened up exciting possibilities while raising important questions about the future of technology. But how close are we to realising this potential, and what can quantum computers actually do today?

This panel brings together Shankar Kumar Selvaraja from the Indian Institute of Science, Quanfluence co-founder Biman Chattopadhyay, and Science writer Debdutta Paul to explore the current state of quantum computing and its possibilities. The conversation goes beyond the hype to explore where quantum computing stands today, what lies on the horizon, and how this emerging technology might change the way we solve some of the world's most complex problems.

name: A Cup of Coffee in a Changing World
description:
Coffee connects us to some of the world's most biodiverse landscapes and to millions of smallholder farmers whose livelihoods depend on them. Yet these landscapes and communities are increasingly vulnerable to a changing climate and the pressures of global markets.

Drawing on a decade of experience building Black Baza Coffee Co. and working with smallholder coffee producers across India, Arshiya Bose explores the complex relationships between agriculture, forests, livelihoods and conservation. From questioning conventional ideas of sustainability to experimenting with ways of making conservation economically viable, this public lecture invites us to think differently about where our coffee comes from, the people who grow it, and our relationship with the natural world.

name: Young Birder's City Council
description:
What would you do if you were responsible for making Bengaluru a safer city for birds?

At the Young Birders' City Council, you get to step into the shoes of conservation problem-solvers. Through real-life challenges faced by birds in our city, you will work in small teams to understand problems and develop solutions.

From designing awareness campaigns and school initiatives to proposing new ideas, policies or practical interventions, each team will get to approach its challenge in its own way. You will get to present your recommendations to the council and will be exposed to different kinds of creative thinking. Join Subiksha Venkatesh for an opportunity to think critically, to collaborate and to imagine a Bengaluru where people and birds can coexist.

name: Metabolic Living: Food, Fat, and the Absorption of Illness in India
description:
In this co-read, we will discuss excerpts from Harris Solomon’s *Metabolic Living* to examine how biomedical values around food come to terms with familial demands, and how gendered duties, such as that of the housewife, are implicated in this. Who is held responsible for the complex, often paradoxical traversing between personal preferences, traditions, and modern health in a rapidly urbanising food culture? 

Examining this through an anthropological lens, this co-read invites us all to share and re-examine our relationship with women and the ‘healthy’ Indian family.

name: Tetris at the Gate of Fate: When Quantum Blocks Refuse to Decide
description:
What if the falling blocks in *Tetris* hadn’t decided what shape they were until you looked?

Quantum computers are often described as ‘faster computers’, but they actually run on stranger rules: superposition, entanglement, and the moment a measurement settles what was uncertain. In this talk, Bhaskaran Muralidharan explains those ideas through a game almost everyone has played. He shows how quantum algorithms use these effects to solve problems that defeat ordinary machines, then introduces his new work, *Gate of Fate*, a quantum version of *Tetris* where every move is a gamble with the laws of physics.

No physics background is needed. Just bring your curiosity and your *Tetris* instincts.

This programme is organised as a part of Bengaluru Jatre.

name: Porous Matter
description:
*Porous Matter* is an interdisciplinary performance by Swiss choreographer Anna Anderegg. The performance emerged from a year-long residency at the Art x Science Office of the University of Zurich, in dialogue with scientists from fields ranging from microbiology to palaeontology. It explores the permeability—the porosity—of the body and its relationship to the more-than-human world, asking: What if we were to understand the body not as a closed organism, but as an open network of relations?

The performance conceives of the body as a living community inhabited by microbes, fungi, and cell colonies that shape our metabolism, our perception, and our very being. Through the interplay of movement, video, mirrors, and sound textures, the performers’ bodies merge with digital structures, creating an immersive space that transforms like a living membrane.

The performance is part of Planetary Embassy, a global Swissnex initiative exploring new forms of diplomacy with the more-than-human world, inviting us to reconsider how we relate to and coexist with other forms of life.

name: When Atoms Compute
description:
Quantum mechanics governs nature at its smallest scales, yet today, scientists can actively engineer this hidden world by controlling entanglement—the unique phenomenon linking quantum particles. Using precisely tuned lasers to manipulate individual atoms, researchers are building programmable quantum machines capable of solving problems beyond the reach of conventional supercomputers, designing new materials, and measuring the world with unprecedented precision. 

Join Peter Zoller for a talk exploring how these atom-based technologies work. He will share highlights from current breakthroughs and look ahead to the next generation of quantum sensors.
